title: Wringer attestation
description: `attestation.json` — the provenance claim `wring attest` assembles and `wring audit` checks, offline, by someone who trusts nobody involved. It says: change C was authorized by spec S, proven by gates G with recorded results against tree T, judged against rubric R with verdict V, and delivered as branch B — and every bundle backing those clauses is byte-identical to when it was written. A clause whose inputs are absent is ABSENT, not invented: an attestation over a bare `wring verify` bundle carries `proven_by` alone and is still worth having. Bundles link to each other by path; this file re-anchors them by digest, recording the sha256 of each one's digests.json, so from the moment it is written the linkage is content-addressed. v0 attestations are UNSIGNED and say so in their own `limits` array — a signature, if one ever arrives, is the sibling file `attestation.json.sig`, never a field in here, so that signing stays purely additive and every existing attestation remains valid byte-for-byte.

attestation_id.description: A run id: `20260806-090348-1029`. Do not parse it for a timestamp; `created_at` is the field that carries one unambiguously.

created_at.description: Local time with UTC offset, seconds resolution.

signature.description: Always null in v0, by ruling, and the artifact says so in `limits`. A signature is a SIBLING file (`attestation.json.sig`), never a field inside a signed payload — embedding one would require canonicalising this JSON before signing, a class of bug with a long history, and would invalidate every attestation written before it existed.

limits.description: What this attestation does NOT claim, in its own words, in the file itself. The first entry is fixed text about being unsigned, and `wring audit` REFUSES an attestation whose limits have been removed: a green artifact that has had its own caveats stripped reads as a stronger claim than it is, which is the vacuity failure in a new costume.

change.description: The commit this attestation is about — the delivered commit where there is one, otherwise the commit the gates ran against.

commit_signature.description: What git says about that commit's signature, recorded as a FACT and never judged. Wringer touches no key and consults no trust store — that is the verifier's job and their trust root. `wring audit` reports this and does not re-verify it, which is what keeps `audit` runnable on a plane.

status.description: git's `%G?` verbatim: G good, B bad, U good-but-untrusted, X expired, Y expired key, R revoked key, E unverifiable, N none. Null only when no commit is named.

signer.description: git's `%GS`, the signer git reports. Null when there is none.

means.description: A plain-English gloss of `status`, so a reader of the artifact does not have to know git's alphabet. A courtesy, not an interpretation.

authorized_by.description: ABSENT when no spec authorised the change. Present only when `wringer.spec.yaml` exists AND says `approved: true` — attest LOADS the spec rather than hashing it blind, because `spec_sha256` hashes the file without parsing it and an unapproved spec hashes exactly like an approved one.

proven_by.description: The run bundle: which tree the gates ran against, and what they returned. Always present — an attestation with nothing proven is not one.

judged_by.description: ABSENT when no verdict about THIS run exists. Matched on the verdict's own `evidence_dir`, never on which verdict is newest: a verdict about a different change is worse than no verdict. A dry-run verdict is refused rather than recorded — nothing was judged, so the clause would be theatre.

delivered_as.description: ABSENT when the anchor was a run rather than a delivery. `mode` is `dry_run` for a delivery that was planned and not sent, which is a real and attestable state: the plan existed and the branch did not.

bundles.description: Every bundle this attestation rests on, re-anchored by content. `digests_sha256` is the sha256 of that bundle's own digests.json FILE — which is what turns a path-linked chain into a content-addressed one, and what makes a self-consistently rewritten bundle (files AND record rewritten together) still fail an audit.
